events.continuity_hook: Closes out the Denver conference plan after the lodging decision from the cancellation-deadline session.
events.interaction_goal: Lock the Denver arrival route, confirm the partner-gym access window, set the Friday lab check-in plan, and make sure the earlier Sunday afternoon return still leaves enough time for checkout and airport transfer.
events.scenario_brief: In the final week before the Denver conference, Kara keeps the suite hotel because the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, and room reliability remain clearer than the reopened venue block. The conference app now routes lab faculty through a separate educator check-in desk, and the hotel confirms partner-gym access for the first night while its fitness room is closed. The Wednesday flight and Sunday afternoon return are still workable, but the airport-to-hotel route, first-night food plan, Friday lab check-in timing, and Sunday checkout buffer still need tightening.

events.continuity_hook: Starts the next clinic-training episode after the larger Denver conference wraps and fall work travel continues.
events.interaction_goal: Build a practical flight-and-hotel shortlist, compare the close clinic-rate hotel against the more reliable suite property, and identify what the clinic must confirm about Wednesday observations, demo storage, and end times.
events.scenario_brief: After returning from Denver, Kara is asked to run a mid-November Monday-Tuesday clinic-training visit for a pediatric therapy group near Raleigh-Durham. The clinic wants a Sunday arrival, two early teaching days, and possibly a short Wednesday morning observation block if the staff lead can arrange it. Flight choices split between a Sunday afternoon nonstop into RDU and a cheaper late connection, while return options depend on whether Tuesday ends cleanly or Wednesday is needed. The closest clinic-rate hotel has uneven recent ratings and unclear fridge availability; a better-rated suite property 15 minutes away confirms a queen room, in-room coffee, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room, but no hot tub.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Raleigh planning once the clinic clarifies that the visit extends into Wednesday morning.
events.interaction_goal: Book the Sunday outbound and Wednesday afternoon return, choose between rental car and rideshare, reserve the reliable suite hotel, and select a window seat where the airline allows seat choice at booking.
events.scenario_brief: The Raleigh clinic confirms that Kara should plan to stay through a short Wednesday morning observation and that Tuesday debrief could run until 4:30 p.m. The Sunday afternoon nonstop is still available, and a Wednesday afternoon return to Tampa avoids a rushed Tuesday evening airport run. The suite hotel holds the clearest room setup and better ratings, while the clinic-rate hotel still cannot confirm the in-room refrigerator. A compact rental car is priced close to rideshare estimates because of the hotel-to-clinic commute.

events.continuity_hook: Revisits the Raleigh lodging and morning logistics after a hotel amenity change and final clinic access instructions arrive.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether the pool closure is worth changing hotels, set Monday and Tuesday departure times from the hotel, and confirm the easiest plan for parking, demo-bag drop-off, and simple room provisions after arrival.
events.scenario_brief: A week before the Raleigh trip, the booked suite hotel emails that its indoor pool will be closed for maintenance during Kara's stay, though the fitness room and confirmed in-room amenities remain available. A same-brand property farther from the clinic has both a pool and hot tub but lower recent ratings, higher parking, and a longer morning drive. The clinic also sends final access details for the therapy gym, including a staff-only entrance for the demo bag and a request that Kara arrive earlier than first planned on Monday.

events.continuity_hook: Starts the next seminar-weekend episode as Kara’s late-fall teaching calendar adds one more course before the holidays.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the Nashville flight patterns, weigh the close hospital-rate hotel against the more predictable suite setup, and list the host details still needed for Thursday access, Saturday teardown, and equipment storage.
events.scenario_brief: Soon after the Raleigh clinic visit, a children's rehab center in Nashville asks Kara to teach a Friday-Saturday pediatric gait seminar in early December. She needs to arrive Thursday with enough time for a room layout check, and Saturday teardown may run close to 5:00 p.m. Flight options include a convenient Thursday afternoon nonstop from Tampa, a cheaper connection arriving late, and return choices that make Sunday afternoon much safer than Saturday evening. The hospital-rate hotel is closest but lists run-of-house bedding and cannot confirm a refrigerator; a better-rated West End suite hotel confirms a queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, fitness room, and indoor pool, but no hot tub and paid parking.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Nashville seminar plan once the host confirms access windows and the travel choices are ready for booking.
events.interaction_goal: Book the Thursday nonstop and Sunday afternoon return, reserve the West End suite hotel if the cancellation terms are acceptable, choose a window seat where available, and note the parking and missing hot tub trade-offs before committing.
events.scenario_brief: The Nashville host confirms Kara can access the teaching room until 7:00 p.m. Thursday and can leave a rolling demo bag locked in the rehab office overnight. Saturday teardown is expected to finish by 4:45 p.m., making the Sunday afternoon return the practical choice. The West End suite hotel still has the clearer queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, fitness access, and indoor pool, while the hospital-rate option remains uncertain on bedding and fridge. The Thursday nonstop has gone up slightly but still protects the room check better than the late connection.
